subject: Archival windows & selective redaction — guidance for MedWorks (PHI in EU)
content:
From: Elena Ramos <elena.ramos@medworks.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: MedWorks Security <security@medworks.com>, procurement@medworks.com
Date: Tue, 02 Mar 2027 08:15:00 +0100
Subject: Retention limits & redaction approach for EU PHI

Hi Marcus,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Two security questions came up from our privacy & procurement teams that we need clarified before we move to contract:

1) Retention windows: For PHI-containing payloads (clinical notes, device telemetry with identifiers), what retention windows do you offer out-of-the-box for hosted vs. private deployments? We need both typical defaults and the options for shorter retention (e.g., 30/90/365 days) and how immutable/backups are handled.

2) Redaction options: We need to understand options for deterministic pseudonymization (reversible vs. irreversible), in-flight redaction patterns (PII regexes), and whether you support redaction-at-rest before backups/archives. Also: how erasure requests propagate to backups and audit trails.

Can you send a short matrix that maps deployment type -> retention behavior -> redaction tools + SLA for guaranteed deletion?

Appreciate it — we have a security review scheduled for Friday and would like something we can circulate.

Best,
Elena Ramos
Head of Procurement, MedWorks Ltd.

-----
Reply 1:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ramos <elena.ramos@medworks.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, MedWorks Security <security@medworks.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Mar 2027 10:02:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Retention limits & redaction approach for EU PHI

Elena —

Thanks for the clear ask. I put a short executive summary below and attached a compact matrix (redwood-retention-redaction-matrix.xlsx) with specifics by deployment mode. High-level:

- Hosted (Redwood API): default retention for request logs + debug traces is 90 days; customer content (input/output) retention is configurable and we offer 30/90/365-day presets. Backups are kept in encrypted snapshots for 90 days by default; hard-delete requests trigger our deletion workflow but snapshot windows mean full removal from all backups can take up to 30 days beyond the deletion request (we track this in an audit log).

- Dedicated (reserved capacity): retention defaults mirror hosted but can be shortened contractually. Snapshots are customer-isolated; we can implement a 30-day snapshot horizon for contracts that require it.

- Private (VPC / on-prem): you control retention and backups. Redwood provides the deletion tooling and guidance; for on-prem we can ship a redaction pipeline that runs in your cluster and purges tokens immediately (configurable).

Redaction and pseudonymization options we support:
- Deterministic irreversible hashing (SHA-256 salted) for IDs — useful when you must prevent re-identification.
- Reversible tokenization via customer-managed KMS for scenarios where re-linking is needed (audit with controlled access).
- Pattern-based redaction (configurable regex sets) applied in-flight or at ingest; can be layered with ML-based name/entity detectors for better recall.
- Selective redaction at rest: we can run an internal redaction pass before object archival in hosted deployments (requires opt-in).

SLA for deletion: For hosted we commit to starting the erasure workflow within 48 hours of a verified request. Final removal from all active stores is usually within 72 hours; removal from immutable snapshots depends on snapshot retention settings (see matrix). For Private deployments we provide tooling and runbooks to achieve immediate deletion within your environment (contractual).

I'll ask Soojin to follow up with the technical redaction details and a note on audit trails. Attaching the matrix now.

Cheers,
Marcus
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-retention-redaction-matrix.xlsx

Reply 2 (technical deep-dive):
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ramos <elena.ramos@medworks.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, MedWorks Security <security@medworks.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Mar 2027 09:34:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Retention limits & redaction approach for EU PHI

Hi Elena —

Quick technical follow-up with patterns and propagation behavior. Attaching our redaction-patterns-overview.pdf. Key points:

1) Ingest-time vs. at-rest redaction- Ingest-time redaction (recommended for hosted when customers require minimal retention) runs in the request path: PII patterns are matched and either masked or tokenized before the data is accepted into long-term store. This guarantees the canonical persistent copy has the redaction applied. Impact: small latency delta (~10–30ms) and potential downstream eval/QA considerations.

- At-rest redaction is run as a background job that rewrites objects and can be scheduled to coincide with archival windows. Useful when you need to keep original inputs temporarily for QA then redact before long-term retention.

2) Backup/snapshot propagation- Our backups are snapshot-based. For hosted customers who opt-in to aggressive erasure (30-day final), we keep ephemeral snapshot retention at 30 days and track a deletion token in the backup manifest. The operational guarantee we surface is: once the deletion token is applied, no active store references the object; complete snapshot-free removal follows the snapshot expiry window (documented in the matrix). We log every stage to the audit trail with immutable timestamps.

3) Reversibility & KMS- Reversible tokenization uses AES-GCM with keys in a customer-managed KMS (for Dedicated and Private) or Redwood-managed KMS (hosted). If you require cryptographic separation, we recommend customer KMS so key rotation and key escrow policies are under your control.

4) Auditability & certification- Every erasure event produces an auditable certificate (JSON blob + hash) and a ticket; for enterprise customers we can route these to your SIEM via syslog/forwarder. Also: SOC 2 artifact references and incremental deletion attestation can be included in our Binder for the account.

If you want, we can run a short POC on a non-prod bucket to demonstrate 30-day snapshot horizon + ingest-time redaction — it takes ~5 business days to enable and validate.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Privacy Engineering Lead — Redwood Inference

Attachment: redaction-patterns-overview.pdf

From: Elena Ramos <elena.ramos@medworks.com>

Date: Thu, 04 Mar 2027 11:07:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Retention limits & redaction approach for EU PHI

Thanks Marcus & Soojin — very helpful. A couple of clarifying questions from security:

- For audit logs: if we redact PII from the primary store, do audit logs retain identifiable values for debugging? We need logs to be useful for incident investigation but not contain raw PHI.
- For legal holds: how do you handle cases where a legal hold prevents deletion? Is there an override / escrow process?

Also please confirm approximate timeline & effort for the POC you mentioned and whether the POC can be done in our eu-central-1 region.

Best,
Elena

Reply 4 (clarify and next steps):
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ramos <elena.ramos@medworks.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, MedWorks Security <security@medworks.com>, procurement@medworks.com
Date: Fri, 05 Mar 2027 16:42:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Retention limits & redaction approach for EU PHI

Elena —

Answers inline:

- Audit logs: We separate operational audit trails from application payloads. Audit log entries will contain identifiers only as cryptographic hashes (deterministic salted) by default. For debugging you can opt-in to a reversible token store gated by KMS access control — access to the key is logged and requires a two-person approval in our Console for enterprise tenants.

- Legal holds: We support a legal hold flag that pauses the erasure workflow for specific records. Legal holds are explicit, auditable, and require a documented approval chain. We provide an escrow workflow (export-only snapshot retained in an encrypted container) if legal/finance requires an immutable copy; the escrow is governed by controls and can be disabled via contract.

POC timeline & region: Yes — eu-central-1 is supported. Typical timeline: 2 business days to provision a non-prod tenant + ingest pipeline, 2–3 days to run ingest and enable ingest-time redaction, then 1–2 days of validation. So ~7 business days end-to-end. We will need a short mutual action plan (I can draft) and an NDA/PO in place to get credentials to your environment if you want customer-managed KMS.

Next steps I propose:
1) Marcus to share a 1-page mutual action plan + matrix (today).
2) MedWorks to confirm POC scope and sign the standard SOW/PO (procurement).
3) Redwood to schedule enablement and provide audit templates (Soojin).

I'll attach the matrix again and a doc link to the SOC2 binder for quick review.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call tomorrow if you want to walk through the POC steps.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Link: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1Gx_example_doclink
